text:
elaine: Quick product question — we're iterating on console saved "route views" and need a decision: should saved views persist routing hints (preferred model/quantization/priority) or should those be a separate 'route policy' resource that the UI can attach to a view? also: how do we surface telemetry sampling when someone applies a policy?

sam: lean toward separate route policy object. saved views = filters/columns only. keeps the saved query simple and avoids coupling to rollout state. UI can offer "attach policy" but don't serialize runtime hints in the saved view itself. :+1:

devon: practical ops POV — folks will expect a one-click "pin model" in the UI. that can create a policy behind the scenes. agree with sam on separation, but we need a clear mapping between view_id and policy_id in telemetry. example API sketch:
```json
POST /route-policies
{ "view_id": "1234", "model_hint": "redwood/open-7b-q4", "rollout_pct": 10, "priority": "high" }
```

maye: telemetry note — when a policy is created/applied we should tag traces with both view_id and policy_id. saved view opens alone should not alter sampling. policy apply events should be recorded with sample rate metadata so analytics can compare before/after. also we should show cost delta in the UI preview.

ryan: UX suggestion — preview modal when attaching a policy: show estimated QPS impact, cost delta (tokens / minute), and an option to run a tiny canary ("preview with telemetry sample") at 0.5–1% for 24h. tiny sample helps catch quality regressions. the toggle should wire to the rollout_pct field.

elaine: summary of what I'll implement in console mocks / API doc: saved_view stays pure (filters/cols). attaching a policy creates a route-policy record. UI will show a preview with cost + option for a small telemetry canary. plan to add a subtle badge on saved views that have an attached policy. API surfaces: POST /route-policies, GET /route-policies?view_id=X, and webhook/event on policy_change.

sam: implementation detail — routing engine expects a small policy shape. keep fields minimal: {model_variant, rollout_pct, fallback_model, priority}. avoid embedding large quantization profiles; those should be a named profile reference if needed.

devon: perf note — don't do heavyweight DB joins on every console render. cache view->policy mapping in redis with a TTL and invalidate on policy_change via events. also, store policy_id in the saved_view metadata for fast lookup (not the full policy blob). :thumbsup:

maye: analytics follow-up — we'll need evtype tags like `policy_applied`, `policy_preview`, and `policy_canary_sample` and a consistent sample_window so we can compute pre/post metrics. can we agree on sample defaults? i'd say 1% for preview canary, 5% for initial rollouts unless ops overrides.

elaine: sounds good. i'll write the API contract and update the console mocks. @sam @devon can you ack this approach by EOD? i'll draft the rollout experiment template for maye and ops.

deploy-bot: Draft route-policy API spec pushed to `docs/internal/console-route-policies.md` (PR #4041)

sam: acked. i'll review the PR and add runtime constraints.

devon: acked, will add redis caching hook and the policy change event emitter to runtime.

maye: once we have the schema i'll prepare the eval metric deck to compare quality and cost.
